column11: derived: Bristol Myers generated $39,438mm of free cash flow on $141,500mm of revenue over 2023, 2024 and 2025, a 27.87% margin, against the 30.0% its cost of sales, SG&A and R&D leave. The smallest of these adjustments by some way: the filed lines nearly reconcile already, and the five-year aggregate of 28.5% says the window is not doing the work. Restated before interest: BMY paid $5,100mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2023 to 2025, 3.60% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so the charge falls by that much, from 2.46% to 0.00%. Restated at replacement capex: BMY spent $3,768mm on plant over 2023 to 2025 against $1,883mm of plant depreciation, 1.33% of revenue above what keeps the plant running. Taken at depreciation, the charge stays nil. Restated without one-off cash: BMY's free cash flow over 2023 to 2025 carried $2,357mm of US transition tax (2023 instalment 567mm; 2024 instalment 799mm; 2025 instalment 991mm). None recurs, so the charge stays nil. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 BMY's cash flow statement shows receivables up $1,026mm, inventories up $1,421mm, payables up $380mm, a working capital build of $2,067mm, 1.46% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge was held at nil where the filed figures rebuild it at -4.68%, and stays there.

column12: BMS's own filed figure across its whole US book, not Krazati's, and for this product it is probably too deep: the aggregate is weighted by Eliquis and Revlimid, which carry Medicaid and Part D rebates a biomarker-selected oral oncolytic does not. A Krazati-specific net was looked for and not found. What the product's own data give is a point-of-sale discount, not a net: CMS Medicare Part D 2024 (drug_demand) records $69,712,635.09 over 582,380 dosage units, $119.70 a tablet, against the $123.05 WAC a tablet then in force ($22,149.25 / 180 from the North Dakota filing), 2.7% off list. That 2.7% cannot stand as gross_to_net_pct, because CMS Part D spending is gross of every manufacturer rebate and of 340B, which is exactly what this key is meant to deduct; carrying it would claim Krazati keeps 97% of WAC. It is a floor on the discount and nothing more. So the filed company figure stays, with its direction stated: net revenue per patient here is likelier to be understated than overstated, and the open question the two bracketing numbers leave is whether a targeted oral oncolytic rebates anywhere near the company average at all. Replace this the day a Krazati-specific net is published

the programme is finished and failed. KRYSTAL-10 (NCT04793958, 461 patients with KRAS G12C-mutated metastatic colorectal cancer after first-line fluoropyrimidine doublet) missed both its dual primary endpoints, reported at the ESMO Gastrointestinal Cancers Congress 2026: median progression-free survival by blinded independent central review 7.5 months with adagrasib plus cetuximab against 8.1 months with chemotherapy (HR 0.89, 95% CI 0.71 to 1.13, p=0.32), and median overall survival 21.6 against 21.7 months (HR 0.83, 95% CI 0.67 to 1.03, p=0.09) at a minimum 26.4 months of follow-up. Objective response was higher, 47% against 16%, and did not carry the endpoints. The FDA then withdrew the accelerated approval of adagrasib with cetuximab in previously treated KRAS G12C mCRC, and the current label (DailyMed SPL effective 23 October 2026) no longer carries it
